analysis: What changed versus the 7:00 AM brief: the split open held and the Nasdaq leg strengthened (Nasdaq +0.6% at the open to +0.8% mid-morning, S&P +0.2% to +0.3%, Dow steady near -0.6%), so the morning is a tech-led split, not a fade. The clearest change is recovery off the lows: Apple narrowed from -4% premarket to near -2%, Palantir from -6%+ to about -2.5%, Shopify from roughly -16% premarket to about -7% to -10% — dip-buying is cushioning the earnings losers without erasing the sell-the-beat verdict. Chips are the other side of the tape: Nvidia +3%+, AMD +5%, and the semiconductor ETF up nearly 4% into AMD's after-close print, while software (Salesforce -3%, software ETF -1%+) and homebuilders lag — a narrow rotation into semis, not broad risk-on. USAC finally moved on its beat, up about 2.4% mid-morning after a flat open, ahead of its 11:00 a.m. ET call. Signal vs noise: the 10:00 a.m. ET JOLTS/factory-orders data, the USAC call, AMD after the close, and overnight midterm results are today's real catalysts; the Nvidia China-cloud report is unconfirmed by the company and should be treated as fragile until Nvidia or a second outlet confirms it. The 10-year yield ticking up to 4.96% is a mild headwind for the lagging rate-sensitive groups.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Split tape held into mid-morning (IBD live coverage): Dow -0.6% (roughly 300 points), S&P 500 +0.3%, Nasdaq +0.8%; SPY +0.2% after the open, QQQ +0.6%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The open's split did not resolve — blue-chip drag versus tech strength, so no broad risk-on or risk-off read yet.

headlines.headline: Apple narrowed its loss to near -2% in morning trading (IBD), after plunging 4% premarket on its December-quarter gross-margin guide of 45-46% (vs 47.9% in September, rising memory costs cited), despite fiscal Q4 EPS $2.10 vs $1.99 expected and sales $114.5B vs $113.4B expected; live quotes showed about -3.0% (Finnhub).
headlines.why_it_matters: Buyers are cushioning the margin-guide selloff but not reversing it — the holiday-quarter margin story still sets the price.

headlines.headline: Chips led the morning: Nvidia up more than 3%, on pace to snap a four-day losing streak; AMD up about 5% in live trading (Finnhub) ahead of its after-close print (EPS $1.95 on $13.1B expected); the SPDR S&P Semiconductor ETF surged nearly 4%, with Sandisk up nearly 7% and Monolithic Power over 5%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The most beaten-down group is leading the tape into AMD's print — that report decides whether this is a bounce or a reversal.

headlines.headline: Nvidia reportedly told cloud partners to sell at least 51% of services to non-Chinese companies under future contracts, per the Financial Times (citing five people familiar); Nvidia neither confirmed nor denied the report, existing contracts are exempt, and a follow-up report said the guidance was not being enforced as a mandatory restriction.
headlines.why_it_matters: Single-source, unconfirmed — treat as fragile: if confirmed, it caps a China-demand channel for future contracts; if softened, it is noise on top of a chip bounce.

headlines.headline: Palantir narrowed its drop to about -2.5% in live trading (Finnhub) from -6%+ premarket, after beating Q3 earnings and revenue targets as new contract value fell to $2.9B from $3.4B; on pace for a sixth straight losing session after breaking its 50-day line Monday (IBD).
headlines.why_it_matters: Another beat sold on a deceleration metric, but the halved loss shows dip-buying — the downtrend is easing, not broken.

headlines.headline: Shopify narrowed its plunge to about -7.3% in live trading (Finnhub), near -10% in IBD's morning action, from roughly -16% premarket after Q3 revenue of $3.74B narrowly missed estimates — its first miss since 2022 — with subscription revenue and merchandise volume also disappointing.
headlines.why_it_matters: The morning's biggest earnings loser is recovering off its lows — the size of the bounce off the open is the sentiment tell for the rest of the session.

headlines.headline: Megacaps split in morning trading (live quotes): Meta +2.06%, Microsoft +1.61%, Amazon +0.36%, Alphabet -0.5%, Tesla -0.54% versus Monday's close (Finnhub/MarketBeat).
headlines.why_it_matters: No single megacap direction — Meta/Microsoft strength offsets Tesla/Alphabet softness, consistent with the split index tape.

headlines.headline: Software lagged while semis rallied: Salesforce was the Dow's furthest laggard at almost -3% (IBD), and the SPDR S&P Software & Services ETF fell more than 1%; biotech and pharma ETFs gained roughly 2% each, while homebuilders fell more than 1%.
headlines.why_it_matters: Sector split confirms the bounce is narrow — semis and biotech up, software and rate-sensitive homebuilders down.

headlines.headline: Midterms today, macro at 10:00 a.m. ET: September JOLTS job openings (7.1M expected vs 7.09M prior) and factory orders (+1.1% expected vs +0.1% prior); polls favor Democrats retaking the House, Polymarket puts Democrats at 78% for the Senate and 95% for the House (IBD). Oil eased to ~$95.85 WTI mid-morning after the premarket rebound faded.
headlines.why_it_matters: Results emerge overnight, so traders carry election risk with no scheduled announcement to trade against; the 10:00 a.m. ET data is the next scheduled catalyst.

headlines.headline: Nasdaq-100 still in correction: Monday's close was more than 10% below its October 6 record, its third correction of 2026, with the semiconductor benchmark down ~12% in three sessions (carried from the 6:00 AM brief).
headlines.why_it_matters: Correction status frames every tech bounce as guilty-until-proven-innocent — AMD after the bell is the next proof point.

usac.headline: USA Compression Partners moved on its Q3 beat in morning trading: shares up about 2.4% to $25.40 at 10:08 a.m. ET (StockAnalysis) after opening flat at $24.80, following this morning's Q3 print of revenue $357.2M (vs $250.3M a year ago and ~$348.32M consensus), Adjusted EBITDA $197.3M, DCF coverage 1.67x, and EPS $0.33 in line with consensus; distribution held at $0.525.
usac.why_it_matters: The revenue beat finally translated into price action after a flat open — the 11:00 a.m. ET call is the next chance for the print to extend or fade.
